blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Pacific Douglas. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Pacific Douglas, South Surrey and White Rock: 25 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 4 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. By listings that is number 6 of 9 South Surrey and White Rock communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the South Surrey and White Rock total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Pacific Douglas rose from 22 in June to 25 in September (+13.6%), and 11 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 4.2% of South Surrey and White Rock’s 593 condos and townhomes listed.

blocks.text: Pacific Douglas home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

34 townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas with a median price of $825,000 (the middle half sold between $748,875 and $873,000), taking a median of 19 days to sell at 97.2% of the last list price; 0% sold above list. They had a median $531 per square foot, a median year built of 2018 and a median strata fee of $380 a month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in Pacific Douglas
Summerfield

is a detached-house subdivision name on the feed (a current listing describes a four-bedroom house "Welcome to Summerfield!" on 172 Street) — detached freehold houses, not a strata complex, and no Summerfield condo building exists to count.

The feed labels its card "Pacific Douglas," but the project's own listing text describes it as being in "South Surrey's Grandview Heights neighbourhood," and its estimated completion ("early 2028") is listing copy only.
Streets, schools and getting around Pacific Douglas

items.t: Every visible card is labelled with the board sub-area "Pacific Douglas" and a Surrey mailing address, on streets including 18 Avenue, 19th Avenue, 172 Street, 172a Street, 1 Avenue, 171a Street and 4 Avenue — the City of Surrey's Douglas neighbourhood at the south end of South Surrey, between the two border crossings, so City of Surrey rules govern, NOT the City of White Rock's.

City plan area: the Douglas plan "encompass[es] an area of approximately 61 hectares (150 acres), generally located east of Hwy 99, west of Hwy 15 and north of the United States," bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve and the Glades Garden Park to the north; the planning process concluded in 1999, and Douglas's land use designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan update. The board sub-area's feed reaches addresses north of the old NCP pocket (18/19 Avenues, 4 Avenue), so the NCP area and the board sub-area are different geographies; the street-level board boundary is UNVERIFIED — FVREB publishes none.
Where condo stock concentrates: it barely does, in apartment form. SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.

Market figures — the sub-area's own (inventory / solds / sales ratio), September 2026: Detached 39 / 6 / 15% (the second-highest published detached ratio in S Surrey White Rock that month, behind Hazelmere at 29%); Condos & Townhomes 25 / 4 / 16%. Community context only — NOT Pacific Douglas figures: S Surrey White Rock detached median $1,628,000 and attached median $700,000 for September 2026; per-sub-area medians are NOT published. SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.

Border crossings and health care: the neighbourhood sits between the Peace Arch crossing (Highway 99, west edge) and the Pacific crossing (Highway 15 / 176 Street, east edge), per the City of Surrey; crossing hours, wait times and NEXUS specifics are UNVERIFIED — no CBSA or Province page was opened in the research. Peace Arch Hospital, 15521 Russell Avenue, White Rock, is a Fraser Health community hospital providing emergency, surgery and maternity care, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Pacific Douglas

items.t: Surrey suites, coach houses and short-term rentals (non-ALR ground): one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable area, not within a coach house or garden suite; coach houses and garden suites 35–75 m², rising to 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the existing house or duplex is below maximum FAR. Short-term rentals: under 90 consecutive days per patron, only the owner may host from their primary residence, tenants cannot run one, and a business licence at $358 per year is required.

ALR frame for the north edge: the plan area is bordered by the Agricultural Land Reserve to the north. On ALR parcels the ALC housing frame is one principal residence at a maximum of 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and subdivision — including depositing a strata plan — requires Agricultural Land Commission permission outside limited exceptions. Which specific parcels are in the ALR: UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel on ALC mapping.

Pad rents (MHPTA) — wherever a park is discussed for this ground: manufactured-home pad rent increases are capped at 2.3% plus the proportional amount for 2026, and 2.2% plus the proportional amount for 2027. No park in-area is named in; the cap is stated so a park unit surfaced under this label is not mistaken for strata stock.

blocks.text: Good to know about Pacific Douglas

items.t: The 1999 plan still quoted in listings no longer governs. The Douglas NCP's designations were superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update — yet a cluster of five feed listings at 148–192 172 Street quotes the NCP "Commercial/Residential" designation and an OCP "Urban" designation for the corner assembly (listing copy only; the current designation for those parcels is UNVERIFIED). Read development value off the in-force OCP and Bylaw 12000 zone for the parcel, not the listing text.

The board sub-area is bigger than the City neighbourhood. The City's Douglas plan area is about 61 hectares east of Highway 99, west of Highway 15 and north of the border — but the board feed under "Pacific Douglas" reaches 18/19 Avenue and 4 Avenue addresses well north of that pocket (Berkeley Village at 16433 19 Avenue among them, with listing sources split between Pacific Douglas and Grandview filings). A "Pacific Douglas" label is a board filing, not a City boundary.

Sewer coverage here has a dated, partial official record. A 2007 City corporate report on the Douglas NCP states a City sanitary sewer system services about half the lands within the Douglas neighbourhood, primarily the more developed southwest area, flowing to the Douglas sanitary pump station. That statement is from 2007; current parcel-level servicing (City water/sewer vs well/septic) is UNVERIFIED — a material check on the area's older streets.

The five-lot 172 Street cluster is one negotiation, not five listings. The feed cards at 148, 158, 172, 186 and 192 172 Street are each marketed as part of an assembly whose neighbours are also for sale — diligence and pricing should run on the combined parcel set and its current OCP/zoning position, not on any single lot's asking figure (listing prices are feed data and are not frozen here).
No official source in this research verifies a border wait-time claim.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Pacific Douglas?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 25 condos and townhomes listed in Pacific Douglas. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Pacific Douglas a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Pacific Douglas had a sales ratio of 16%, which the reports’ scale reads as a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 11 condos and townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas over those 4 months, out of 375 in all of South Surrey and White Rock.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did townhomes in Pacific Douglas sell for?
faq.a: 34 townhomes sold in Pacific Douglas between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $825,000.

faq.q: How long do townhomes take to sell in Pacific Douglas?
faq.a: The median was 19 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.2% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: How did Pacific Douglas sell in September 2026?
faq.a: No sub-area median is published, and the community medians (detached $1,628,000; attached $700,000) are not Pacific Douglas figures. SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: Which plan guides land use in Douglas now?
faq.a: The Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026) — the City states the Douglas plan's land use designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP update, with zoning under Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000.

faq.q: Can I rent out a townhome at Douglas Point or Berkeley Village long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC.

faq.q: Which elementary school is in the neighbourhood?
faq.a: Catchment assignment for a specific home address is UNVERIFIED, so check the exact address with the district before relying on it.

faq.q: Does a Douglas Green Living purchase work like a resale?
faq.a: No. While it is a presale it is a developer contract: REDMA s. 21 gives a 7-day rescission period from the later of signing and acknowledging the disclosure statement, deposits are held in trust under s. 18, and 5% GST applies to the new construction (subject to the rebates in). Its completion timing is UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: Is Douglas Point a seniors complex?
A listing quotes a Douglas NCP designation — can I rely on it for development potential?
faq.a: No. The 1999 Douglas NCP designations have been superseded by the Surrey 2050 OCP (Bylaw No. 21900, adopted June 15, 2026); check the in-force OCP designation and the Bylaw No. 12000 zone for the specific PID.

faq.q: How big can a secondary suite be in Surrey?
faq.a: One suite per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable area under Zoning By-law No. 12000.
